Chapter 1: The Cost of Chasing Approval and Constant Activity
Have you ever felt a kind of exhaustion that goes way deeper than just being physically tired?
It’s not from running a marathon, or staying up all night caring for someone you love.
Instead, it’s that worn-out feeling that creeps in after years of trying to be everything for everyone—always saying yes, always pushing yourself, always hoping that the next achievement will finally bring some peace.
So many of us get caught in this cycle. We start to believe that being busy is something to be proud of. That if other people need us, then we must be loved.
Picture this: there’s a woman whose days all blur together in a nonstop stream of commitments. She’s the one people count on—the one who never misses a deadline, shows up with a smile, and somehow juggles work, family, friendships, and even community obligations.
From the outside, she looks like she’s got it all together. But inside? She feels empty. It’s as if her energy and joy are slowly draining away with every new demand.
It’s really easy to slip into that pattern, isn’t it? The world seems to reward those who keep their schedules packed, who never let anyone down.
But here’s something to pay attention to: underneath all that hustle, we start to lose something important. When you’re always striving, there’s hardly any space left for rest, for reflection, or for real connection with the people who matter most.
The heart goes numb. The soul starts to feel like a stranger.
One evening, after yet another day jam-packed with meetings and errands, this woman sits alone in her car. Her hands grip the steering wheel. And suddenly, she can’t even remember the last time she felt truly present—really alive in her own life.
That realization hits hard: all this effort, all this running around, hasn’t brought her closer to the life she wanted. If anything, it’s pulled her further away—from herself, and from the people she loves.
Most of us don’t notice that slow drift at first. The calendar just keeps filling up. The inbox is always overflowing. And that sense of purpose we once had? It gets replaced by a relentless urge to keep up, to never let anyone down.
The fear of disappointing others quietly takes the wheel, pushing us further and further until there’s nothing left to give.
But in the quiet moments—when you finally catch your breath—the truth bubbles up. Chasing perfection and approval? It’s a losing game. No matter how much you accomplish, it never feels like enough.
And the cost? It’s steep. Relationships get shallow. Creativity dries up. Even the simple joys—like laughing around the dinner table or taking a walk in the woods—start to feel rare.
Letting go of this way of living isn’t easy. It means facing the discomfort of saying no, of letting people down, of realizing that being busy isn’t the same as being valuable.
But in that discomfort, there’s a chance—a real chance—to rediscover what matters most.
So, the journey really begins with a single, honest question:
What if the life that looks so impressive from the outside is actually keeping your heart locked away?
